title: The Knuckleheads: a playable Godot speed platformer built with AI assistance
author: tkbillington
selftext:
I’m a software engineer exploring game development, and I’ve released a free prototype of a Sonic-inspired pirate platformer called The Knuckleheads.

I used Godot and Codex, alongside AI-generated assets, Photoshop editing, and repeated playtesting with suggestions. The idea grew out of playing the classic 2D Sonic games with my son. We have played through them all multiple times and I wanted to keep that fun alive and going, and yes, he thought the demo level was cool.

One important lesson that stuck out has been how much work comes after something technically functions in refinement and fitting it into the theme. The boulder chase worked, but testers didn’t understand when to slide, and some scripted jumps felt unnatural. Their feedback led to clearer signs and more playable jumps. Character rigging and the transitions between paths also needed repeated passes. It can be a great vision and video game element, but it can be tougher to fit into a specific game than it initially seems once you have some decisions made.

The 30-second trailer is in this post and [**the demo is free in a desktop browser**](https://peanutthedog1985.itch.io/the-knuckleheads-spike-island). Hopefully you have a controller or two plugged in for co-op. I really want to do more with the co-op in the future.

I’m looking for fresh eyes on the controls, pacing, and fairness. I’m also happy to discuss where the AI-assisted workflow helped and where it needed more iteration. If I get more positive reception I plan on releasing a more complete game I am visioning now.

  
Before posting this, early testing feedback has been...

* Too many shields/Shields are sort of confusing
* Too long/boring/many mechanics in tutorial
* Game is too hard
* It's a lot of fun when it works
* Cute and silly enjoyable graphics and retro feel
* Controls feel nice when it makes sense
